title: New Employee Technology Onboarding
scenario: HR submits a request to onboard Ms. Patel, a new 6th-grade math teacher, starting in 9 business days. She will need a MacBook, an iPad, a Google Workspace account with the Faculty OU, a school phone extension, building access badge, and the standard faculty app set. Her classroom is 12C and her mentor is Mrs. Hayes.
impact: Operational: a delay in onboarding means Ms. Patel arrives on her first day unable to teach. A confused first day creates a poor impression and creates support burden across the IT team.
objectives: Confirm the full onboarding checklist with HR and the hiring manager
Create the user accounts in the directory and Google Workspace with the correct OU
Stage the device images, enroll them in MDM, and assign them to the user
Test all credentials and device logins before the start date
Prepare a personalized welcome packet and first-day checklist
Conduct a 30-minute welcome walkthrough on her first morning

evidence.description: Confirmation of directory account, Google Workspace OU, and MFA enrollment
Devices staged with asset tags, MDM enrolled, and assigned to the user
Personalized welcome packet with credentials, device serial numbers, and contacts

decisionPoints.prompt: What is the correct order of operations for creating a new employee's accounts?

options.label: Create the Google Workspace account first because most school apps depend on it
options.feedback: Google Workspace is the front end, but the directory is the back end. Create the directory account first so GWS can sync from it.

options.label: Create the directory account first, then sync to Google Workspace, then enable MFA and OU assignment
options.feedback: Correct — directory first, then downstream systems, then MFA. Skipping order causes orphaned accounts and permission drift.

options.label: Create all accounts simultaneously in each system to save time
options.feedback: Simultaneous creation without the directory anchor produces duplicates and inconsistent permission models. Always anchor on the directory.

decisionPoints.prompt: Ms. Patel's first day is Monday at 8:00 AM. She has 30 minutes with you before class. What is the most valuable use of that time?

options.label: Walk her through the entire acceptable use policy and security training slides
options.feedback: Information-dumping on day one overwhelms new employees. Cover AUP essentials only, and send the full training for self-paced completion.

options.label: Practical hands-on: log in, install apps, test the projector, find the shared drive, and meet her mentor
options.feedback: Correct — hands-on practice on day one builds confidence and surfaces issues early. Pair with the mentor for ongoing support.

options.label: Skip the walkthrough — the welcome packet is enough and she can call the help desk
options.feedback: New employees need guided context, not a packet. A 30-minute walkthrough is cheap insurance against a bad first day.

ticket.initialDescription: HR submits onboarding request for Ms. Patel, new 6th-grade math teacher. Start date in 9 business days. Needs MacBook, iPad, Google Workspace account, phone extension, badge, standard faculty app set.

nodes.title: Confirm the onboarding scope
nodes.body: Review the HR request. Confirm the start date, role, mentor, classroom, and the full list of required accounts, devices, and access. Note any special requirements. Update the new user record.

nodes.title: Create the user accounts
nodes.body: Create the directory account first, then sync to Google Workspace and assign the Faculty OU. Enroll MFA. Save the account creation evidence.

nodes.title: Account creation order
nodes.body: Confirm the order of operations. Was the directory created first?

nodes.title: Stage the devices
nodes.body: Image the MacBook and iPad to the school standard, enroll in MDM, assign to the user, and push the faculty app set. Save the staging record as evidence.

nodes.title: Validate the onboarding end-to-end
nodes.body: Log in to the MacBook and iPad as Ms. Patel would, with a test login if needed. Verify Google Workspace, MFA, the standard app set, the phone extension, and the badge. Save the validation evidence.

nodes.title: Plan the welcome walkthrough
nodes.body: Choose the most valuable use of the 30-minute first-day session.

nodes.title: Prepare the welcome packet
nodes.body: Assemble the personalized welcome packet: account details, device serial numbers, mentor contact, building access info, the 30-minute walkthrough agenda, and the help-desk contact.
nodes.prompt: Write the welcome packet content for Ms. Patel. Plain language, friendly tone, clear next steps for her first morning.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review the onboarding. Key lessons: directory-first account creation, stage and validate devices before day one, and invest in a hands-on welcome walkthrough.

kbOpportunity: Faculty onboarding checklist: directory → Google Workspace → MFA → device staging and MDM → standard app set → validation → welcome packet → 30-minute first-day walkthrough → mentor pairing.
